chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: The gangster-run Burnham Inn and the man dead when the lights came on
summary: She made a fortune at the Burnham Inn in Burnham, Illinois, where once the lights went out during her song and a dead man lay there when they came back.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: That's right. And then now, Chris, when I worked in Chicago, there was a place called the Burnham Inn in Burnham, Illinois, and you used to -- we -- a lot of the people used to go out to Burnham, because that was owned by the gangsters.
B-u-r-n-h-a-m, Burnham, Burnham, Illinois. And that was called the Burnham Inn. And that was a place that was run by the gangsters, and we worked -- I worked out there.
Well, was that far from Chicago?

It was a pretty good distance, couple hours or so or more. But I used to -- I used to make that trip just the same, because I made a fortune out there, you know? Made -- that's the place I told you, when the lights went off, the lights went off and came back on, there was a man laying there dead.
Oh, I think you mentioned that.

Yeah. Well, only thing I can say is just when I was singing and the lights suddenly went off, when they came back on, there was the man. I don't know who did it, and I didn't see anything. But I know that's what happened.
